items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-12-09
items.q: And when I walked in, Piku had been playing with her.

ctx.x: Uh, what was, wouldn't Joe consider, what was he like to come from? Joe was always strong ever since I know him. Uh, I'm gonna tell you, I don't remember Joe playing grannery.

Uh, I was a Joe. And I feel that he could play grannery. But, although his hands and fingers were stiff. He'd cut across the hands and, you know, his fingers. Uh, no. And say he was the first stuff and all the way up, he was just black, but he was like an Indian. He was small, he was very good looking boy, I think. And he didn't work much because the majority, I'm not the least mean, the majority of the light-skinned musicians stay together. They stay together. But I can tell you about an incident that happened…

So, the tours of Japan. Do you have any particular memories? I know this is one story which somebody told me, which I'd like you to repeat if you can remember. It's about this time you went to this place in Tokyo, where they had jukebox with, just with George Lewis records on them. And you went there. And you remember that time? Do you remember that time? Yeah, that was the first year of 63. I remember that.

items.title: Alphonse Picou Interview, 1958-04-04
items.q: Did you ever have any business with George Lewis?

ctx.x: Does he play every night, you mean? He plays every night now? No. I wonder if he was on Royal Street, if he played someplace on Royal Street? Yes, he do. But I believe it's three of... About three times a week. Three times a week. Yes.
Did you ever have any business with George Lewis? Did you ever...?

items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-11-01
items.q: every one of them made an impression on me because, excuse me, every one had their own style. I was, uh, Charlie McQuirtis, P. Kool-Eddie's Betts, George Bakke, uh, Lorenzo Teal, uh, Johnny, uh, Johnny Brown

ctx.x: No, I'm concerned, no. Playing lead, this is what you have to do a lot. Yeah. I see. Um... So, let's, I think, something I haven't asked you about is something about, is about the clarinet, you know, you have heard in New Orleans and ones that, you know, that made an impression on you, you know, different clarinet days you had when you were young.

But I tell you, I was a lot of them. But, uh, every one of them made an impression on me because, excuse me, every one had their own style. I was, uh, Charlie McQuirtis, P. Kool-Eddie's Betts, George Bakke, uh, Lorenzo Teal, uh, Johnny, uh, Johnny Brown, and so many others. Zeb, uh, uh, Eddie Sherry, City Sherry, uh, George Boyd, uh, uh, many of them are good clarinet players. Uh, uh, they, uh, some of them didn't read, of course. Uh, George Boyd didn't read any music. Uh, and, uh, a lot of others that didn't…
Uh, uh. Did they have different tones for them? No, they didn't have different tones. Uh, I, I know, uh, I know, uh, uh,
